title: The Sicilian Najdorf — A Master Class

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6
beats.say: The Najdorf — the most respected of all the Sicilians, the choice of champions from Fischer to Kasparov. The quiet-looking a6 is deeply purposeful: it denies White's pieces the b5-square and prepares Black's two great freeing breaks, e5 and b5. From here Black plays for the full point, never a meek draw.
beats.sayShort: a6 — the Najdorf, controlling b5.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 e5
beats.say: Be3 signals the English Attack, White's most dangerous modern try — the plan is f3, Qd2, queenside castling and a pawn avalanche. Black strikes first in the centre with e5, kicking the d4-knight and seizing space. The price is the d5-square; the reward is a free, active game.
beats.sayShort: e5 — grab the centre, kick the knight.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 e5 Nb3 Be6
beats.say: The knight retreats to b3, and Black calmly plugs the hole: Be6 plants the bishop where it guards the sensitive d5-square. This is the bargain Black accepts in the Najdorf — concede d5 as a square, but control it with pieces, and get rapid development and active play in return.
beats.sayShort: Be6 — cover the d5-square.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 e5 Nb3 Be6 f3 Be7 Qd2 O-O
beats.say: White builds the battering ram — f3 braces the e4-pawn and clears the path for g4, while Qd2 connects the rooks for queenside castling. Black develops Be7 and castles, eyes open to the coming kingside storm. The Najdorf deal is struck: Black will race on the queenside while White hurls pawns at the king.
beats.sayShort: f3 and Qd2 — White readies the storm.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 e5 Nb3 Be6 f3 Be7 Qd2 O-O O-O-O Nbd7
beats.say: The kings split — White castles queenside, straight into the path of Black's counterattack. Nbd7 develops with intent: the knight heads for c5 or b6, eyeing the c4 and d5 squares, while Black prepares the thematic b5 and b4 to prise open lines at White's king. Whoever lands first takes the point.
beats.sayShort: Nbd7 — prep the b5 and b4 storm.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 e5 Nb3 Be6 f3 Be7 Qd2 O-O O-O-O Nbd7
beats.say: This is the Najdorf in essence: Black accepts a small structural concession on d5 in exchange for the most dynamic counterplay in all of chess. Against the English Attack the race is brutal and concrete — Black's b5-b4 lever and the half-open c-file hunt White's king while White's g- and h-pawns storm the other way. Master the theory, and Black wins the sharpest battles the game has to offer.
beats.sayShort: Concede d5, win the sharper race.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be2 e5
beats.say: Against the calm Be2 Classical, Black grabs the centre with e5. White will not storm here — it is a positional game, and the whole fight revolves around the d5-square.
beats.sayShort: e5 — claim the centre vs the quiet Be2.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be2 e5 Nb3 Be7 O-O O-O Be3 Be6
beats.say: Both sides develop and castle short. Black's bishop settles on e6, guarding d5; the entire struggle is whether White can plant a piece on that hole or Black can keep it covered.
beats.sayShort: Be6 guards d5; Black is solid.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be2 e5 Nb3 Be7 O-O O-O Be3 Be6 Nd5 Nbd7
beats.say: White occupies the hole with Nd5, but Black is unfazed — Nbd7 develops and prepares to challenge or trade the knight with a later Nxd5. The structure is sound and the position fully equal; Black has the easier plans on the queenside.
beats.sayShort: Nbd7 — challenge the d5-knight, equal.

_key: Najdorf: 6.Bg5 Main Line (with e6 and f4)
title: Najdorf — The 6.Bg5 Main Line

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6
beats.say: The classical 6.Bg5 — White pins the f6-knight and plays for a quick f4 and kingside expansion. Black answers with the flexible e6, building the small, solid centre that has anchored Najdorf players for generations.
beats.sayShort: Bg5 and e6 — the classical main line.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Be7 Qf3 Qc7 O-O-O Nbd7
beats.say: White builds with f4, Qf3 and castles long; Black develops Be7, Qc7 and Nbd7, all pointing at the queenside. The battle lines are drawn: White storms with g4 and g5, Black counters with b5 and b4 down the half-open c-file.
beats.sayShort: Qc7 and Nbd7 — ready the b5 counter.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Be7 Qf3 Qc7 O-O-O Nbd7 g4 b5
beats.say: White lunges g4, Black fires b5 — the two storms are off. Both attacks come at full tilt; in this line a single tempo can decide the game, and Black's queenside play is famously fast.
beats.sayShort: g4 vs b5 — the storms collide.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Be7 Qf3 Qc7 O-O-O Nbd7 g4 b5 Bxf6 Nxf6
beats.say: White trades on f6 to loosen Black's grip and speed the attack, but Nxf6 recaptures naturally and Black's counterplay rolls on, with b4 to follow. A razor-sharp, deeply analysed battlefield where the well-prepared Black player scores heavily.
beats.sayShort: Nxf6 recaptures; b4 comes next.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Qb6
beats.say: The Poisoned Pawn — one of the boldest ideas in all of chess. Instead of quietly defending, Black plays Qb6, attacking the b2-pawn and daring White to prove that the whole attack is worth a single pawn.
beats.sayShort: Qb6 — eye the poisoned b2-pawn.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Qb6 Qd2 Qxb2 Rb1 Qa3
beats.say: White offers it with Qd2; Black snatches — Qxb2! After Rb1 the queen slips out to a3, safe and active. Black is a clean pawn up, and the entire question becomes whether White's lead in development and open lines are real compensation. Decades of analysis say Black holds.
beats.sayShort: Qxb2 then Qa3 — snatch and survive.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Qb6 Qd2 Qxb2 Rb1 Qa3 e5 dxe5 fxe5 Nfd7
beats.say: White strikes with e5 to blow open the centre; Black coolly trades and retreats the knight to d7, untangling. This is the Poisoned Pawn's essence: grab the material, weather the storm with precise defence, and emerge a pawn up into a winning endgame.
beats.sayShort: Nfd7 — untangle, a pawn ahead.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 f3 e5
beats.say: With 6.f3 White heads for the English Attack by a different route, playing f3 before Be3 to sidestep some of Black's options. Black reacts identically — e5, taking the centre and the same active Najdorf game.
beats.sayShort: e5 — meet the f3 move order head-on.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 f3 e5 Nb3 Be6 Be3 Be7
beats.say: The knight drops to b3 and Black plugs the d5-hole with Be6, then develops Be7 — the standard, reliable English Attack setup, reached here by the f3 road.
beats.sayShort: Be6 — cover d5, develop Be7.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 f3 e5 Nb3 Be6 Be3 Be7 Qd2 O-O O-O-O Nbd7
beats.say: White castles long with Qd2 ready; Black castles and plays Nbd7, preparing the b5 and b4 break. The race is on — Black's queenside attack against White's pawn storm, exactly as in the main English Attack.
beats.sayShort: Nbd7 — prep the b5 and b4 break.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bc4 e6
beats.say: The Fischer-Sozin — White throws the bishop to c4, aiming the whole battery at f7 and the e6-square. Black blunts it immediately with e6, building a solid wall and preparing rapid queenside expansion.
beats.sayShort: e6 — wall off the c4-bishop.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bc4 e6 Bb3 Be7 f3 O-O Qe2 b5
beats.say: White retreats the bishop to b3 and prepares to castle long; Black develops and strikes with b5, the thematic Najdorf expansion. The b-pawn comes with tempo, gaining space and eyeing b4 to chase the c3-knight.
beats.sayShort: b5 — the Najdorf queenside expansion.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bc4 e6 Bb3 Be7 f3 O-O Qe2 b5 Be3 b4
beats.say: Be3 develops, and b4 strikes — kicking the c3-knight and opening the b-file and the long diagonal for Black's pieces. Against the Fischer-Sozin's kingside aims, Black's queenside counterattack is fast and concrete.
beats.sayShort: b4 — chase the knight, open lines.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 g3 e5
beats.say: The fianchetto approach — g3 and Bg2, a quiet positional setup aiming the bishop down the long light-square diagonal. Black takes the centre with e5; the knight must retreat awkwardly to e2, and Black reaches an easy game.
beats.sayShort: e5 — punish the slow g3 setup.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 g3 e5 Nde2 Be7 Bg2 O-O O-O Nbd7
beats.say: The knight reroutes via e2, White fianchettoes and castles. Black develops naturally — Be7, short castling, Nbd7 — with comfortable equality and the half-open c-file waiting for later queenside play.
beats.sayShort: Nbd7 — develop, fully comfortable.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 g3 e5 Nde2 Be7 Bg2 O-O O-O Nbd7 a4 Rb8
beats.say: White plays a4 to restrain b5; Black calmly reroutes with Rb8, preparing the b5 break anyway after due preparation. Against the quiet g3 setup Black equalises easily and keeps all the winning chances of a Najdorf structure.
beats.sayShort: Rb8 — prepare b5 despite a4.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 Ng4
beats.say: Against 6.Be3, the immediate Ng4 is a sharp try — Black attacks the bishop at once, trying to provoke a trade or a concession before White can finish building the English Attack.
beats.sayShort: Ng4 — harass the e3-bishop at once.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 Ng4 Bg5 h6 Bh4 g5 Bg3
beats.say: The bishop dodges to g5, but h6 and g5 chase it all the way to g3, gaining big kingside space in the process. Black's pawns roll forward and White's bishop is shut out of the game.
beats.sayShort: h6 and g5 — kick the bishop, grab space.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3 Ng4 Bg5 h6 Bh4 g5 Bg3 Bg7 Qd2 Nc6
beats.say: Black completes the fianchetto with Bg7 — the bishop now rakes the long diagonal — and Nc6 develops, pressing the d4-knight. The Ng4 plan has handed Black space and the freedom of the two bishops: an aggressive, double-edged Najdorf.
beats.sayShort: Bg7 rakes the long diagonal.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 a4 e5
beats.say: With a4 White prevents Black's b5 break before anything else — the Anti-Najdorf. Black shrugs and plays e5, taking the centre; the game becomes a quieter positional Najdorf where Black is completely fine.
beats.sayShort: e5 — a4 stops b5, so grab the centre.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 a4 e5 Nb3 Be7 Be2 O-O O-O Be6
beats.say: Both sides develop quietly and castle short. Black's bishop covers d5 from e6, the structure is rock-solid, and with the b5 break held back Black simply manoeuvres for the central d5 break or play down the c-file instead.
beats.sayShort: Be6 covers d5; Black is solid.

beats.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 a4 e5 Nb3 Be7 Be2 O-O O-O Be6 Be3 Nbd7
beats.say: Be3 and Nbd7 complete the setup. Without the b5 lever Black shifts plans — rerouting the knight toward the c5 outpost or preparing a central d5 break — and keeps a sound, equal game with chances for both sides. The a4-pull cost White a little time, too.
beats.sayShort: Nbd7 — reroute toward c5 and d5.
